title: Relative Segal assembly of symmetric active blocks
statement: Use symmetric operadic families of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] and active concatenation of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. Let $n\geq1$ and let $\pi:M^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^n$ be a small symmetric operadic family. Write $M_0^\otimes$ for its parameter-zero fiber. Let $b$ lie over $(\langle s\rangle,t)$ with $t>0$, choose inert projections $b\to b_j$, and give active arrows $a_j:x_j\to b_j$ with every $x_j$ in $M_0^\otimes$. Choose the concatenation $x=\bigoplus_{j=1}^s x_j$ in $M_0^\otimes$ and its stationary inert block projections $p_j:x\to x_j$. Let $\alpha$ be the pointed map from the concatenated input set to $\langle s\rangle$ sending each input in block $j$ to $j$. The space of arrows $a:x\to b$ over $(\alpha,0\to t)$, equipped with specified component triangles identifying $(b\to b_j)a$ with $a_jp_j$, is contractible. Such $a$ is active. For two tuples $(a_j)$ and $(a'_j)$, coherent triangles $a'_jh_j\simeq a_j$ with $h_j:x_j\to x'_j$ in $M_0^\otimes$ assemble to a coherent triangle $a'(\bigoplus_jh_j)\simeq a$, naturally with respect to paths and all higher simplices of the triangle data. These choices give a coherent functor from the product of the incoming active slices at the $b_j$ to the incoming active slice at $b$. Here an incoming active slice at $c$ has objects active arrows $z\to c$ with $z\in M_0^\otimes$ and simplices the coherent triangles with their higher compatibilities, using the join-slice convention of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Empty blocks and $s=0$ are included.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative cocartesian factorization and blockwise Segal comparison.

proof.text: Write $r_j$ for the input arity of $x_j$, $r=\sum_j r_j$, $\delta_j:b\to b_j$ for the chosen inert edges, $q_j:\langle r\rangle\to\langle r_j\rangle$ for the block projections, and $\kappa_j:\langle r_j\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ for the active fold maps. The specified $p_j$ lie over $(q_j,\mathrm{id}_0)$, and $a_j$ lies over $(\kappa_j,0\to t)$. Thus $a_jp_j$ lies over $(\beta_j,0\to t)$ where $\beta_j=\kappa_jq_j=\rho_j\alpha$. These are the component base maps of $(\alpha,0\to t)$. Stationarity holds because the source and target parameter of $p_j$ are both $0$; the inert edges $\delta_j$ similarly have parameter $\mathrm{id}_t$. This uses the inert-edge convention in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] and the chosen concatenation of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation].

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: For the fixed tuple put $P=\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,b)_{(\alpha,0\to t)}$ and $Q=\prod_j\operatorname{Map}_{M^\otimes}(x,b_j)_{(\beta_j,0\to t)}$, where subscripts denote homotopy fibers over the specified base arrows. Postcomposition with $\delta_j$ gives $E:P\to Q$. The relative Segal homotopy-pullback square in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], applied to $y=x$ and target $b$, identifies $P$ with $Q$: the mapping spaces in the nerve of the ordinary category $\mathrm{Fin}_*\times[n]$ are discrete sets of arrows, and taking the fiber over the single arrow $(\alpha,0\to t)$ gives exactly the displayed product of component fibers. This is a fiberwise application of the stated homotopy-pullback axiom, not an assertion that an unrestricted base mapping space is contractible.

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: The tuple $(a_jp_j)_j$ is a point $v$ of $Q$. An arrow together with the specified component triangles is precisely a point of $\operatorname{hofib}_v(E)$, including its path data. Since $E$ is an equivalence, [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] says this homotopy fiber is contractible; in particular it is nonempty. Every resulting arrow lies over $\alpha$. Its inverse image of the basepoint is just the basepoint, so it is active by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. This proves the objectwise assertion with all higher homotopies of its choices.

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: For coherence let $C=(M_{0,\mathrm{act}}^\otimes)^s$ and let $F:C\to M_{0,\mathrm{act}}^\otimes$ be concatenation. Define contravariant space diagrams on $C$ by $P(\mathbf x)=\operatorname{Map}(F\mathbf x,b)_{(\alpha_{\mathbf x},0\to t)}$, $Q(\mathbf x)=\prod_j\operatorname{Map}(F\mathbf x,b_j)_{(\rho_j\alpha_{\mathbf x},0\to t)}$, and $R(\mathbf x)=\prod_j\operatorname{Map}(x_j,b_j)_{(\kappa_j,0\to t)}$. The coherent mapping bifunctor and its pre/postcomposition compatibilities in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] make these coherent diagrams: an active tuple $\mathbf h$ preserves blocks, so $\alpha_{\mathbf x\prime}F(\mathbf h)=\alpha_{\mathbf x}$. By [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] and [lem-coef-active-concatenation-block-projections], $F(\mathbf h)$ lies over the blockwise sum of the active base maps, and the block projections form coherent transformations $p_j:\iota F\Rightarrow\iota\,\mathrm{pr}_j$, giving the coherent comparisons $p_j\prime F(\mathbf h)\simeq h_jp_j$ with all higher simplices. Therefore composition defines transformations $E:P\to Q$ by $(\delta_j)_j$ and $V:R\to Q$ by $(p_j)_j$, retaining all higher coherences.

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: Each component of $E$ is the equivalence proved in Step 2. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] to $\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$: $E$ is an equivalence there, so choose a coherent inverse $L:Q\to P$ and its inverse homotopies. The transformation $LV:R\to P$ now assigns assembled operations coherently. By the right-fibration classification and mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], it induces a functor between the total right fibrations representing $R$ and $P$, over $C$. The first total category is $\prod_jJ_{b_j}$, since its vertex fibers are the active mapping spaces into the $b_j$ and its transports are precomposition. The second is the subcategory of the pullback $C\times_{M_{0,\mathrm{act}}^\otimes}J_b$ selecting the base maps $\alpha_{\mathbf x}$. The join-slice identification in [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and the representable comparison in the transport statement give these identifications with coherent triangles, not only with homotopy classes. Composing with its projection to $J_b$ is the required functor.

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: The inverse homotopy $E LV\simeq V$ supplies the specified component triangles. For an edge $(h_j,\tau_j)$ of the product slices, its image is an edge over $h=\bigoplus_jh_j$, hence a triangle $a\prime h\simeq a$. Its $j$th component is the path $\delta_j a\prime h\simeq a_j\prime p_j\prime h\simeq a_j\prime h_jp_j\simeq a_jp_j\simeq\delta_j a$. Here the second comparison is the naturality square of [lem-coef-active-concatenation-block-projections] and $\tau_j$ supplies the third. A source-change edge occurring in an incoming active slice is itself active: if a non-basepoint input were killed by $h_j$, the composite with the active $a_j\prime$ would kill it, contradicting activity of $a_j$. Thus every edge of the input slices lies over $C$. Because $LV$ and its comparison with $V$ are coherent transformations and the transport comparison is coherent on mapping spaces, the same formula includes every higher simplex and all its faces and degeneracies.

source.place: Definition 2.3.2.10 and proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.253-254 and 336-337; agent expansion of the blockwise Segal argument.

proof.text: If $s=0$, the category $C$ and the empty products $Q,R$ are terminal, and $F$ selects the empty tuple. The relative Segal axiom at arity zero makes $P\to Q=*$ an equivalence, so the preceding construction gives the functor from the terminal empty product. If an individual $r_j=0$, $q_j$ is still inert (the condition on its non-basepoint outputs is vacuous), $\kappa_j$ is still active, and $\rho_j\alpha=\kappa_jq_j$ still holds. No step used $r_j>0$. For $s=1$ the block projection is the identity up to its specified coherent equivalence, and Step 2 reduces to that equivalence. The empty-unit convention is supplied by [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], and the zero-output mapping-space condition by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family].

split_report.summary: Expanded the relative Segal block assembly into seven steps. Fixed the ill-typed component formula in the interrupted draft and replaced its unsupported coherence assertion with an explicit transformation of contravariant mapping-space diagrams, inverted by the existing pointwise-equivalence theorem and converted to a slice functor by existing space-valued transport. Contractibility is justified by the existing homotopy-fiber criterion. Statement unchanged; no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: The inherited prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison, through HA Theorem 3.1.2.3(1), printed pp.336-337: Steps 1-3 realize relative Segal assembly, Steps 4-6 coherent slice functoriality, and Step 7 the empty-block cases.

tool_uses.why: Step 3 uses only the general characterization of equivalences of spaces by contractible homotopy fibers; this is a homotopy-theoretic tool, not a replacement of the operadic unit route.
